summary_oneline: Most of the brainstorm's 'connections core' already exists in parrot.auth (AbstractOAuth2Manager, OAuth2ProviderRegistry, IntegrationsService, CredentialBroker, Identity Vault owner); the real gap is making connections principal-keyed and channel-neutral: re-key the hot cache off the channel, move Jira onto the generic manager, unify the two needs-auth signals, open a user-level connections view and push completion to channels instead of direct in-process calls.

Jira-specific manager (jira:oauth:{channel}:{user_id}, no PKCE, accessible-resources→cloud_id) with the CredentialSink Protocol for the durable owner; parallel to, not a subclass of, AbstractOAuth2Manager

FEAT-735 decision (2026-10-23): Identity Vault durable owner, Redis live tool path, Slack first-link gap

constraints.statement: The durable owner of the Jira grant is navigator-auth's Identity Vault (auth.user_identities keyed by nav user_id + provider + account), with Redis jira:oauth:{channel}:{user_id} as the live tool path — decided 2026-10-23 (FEAT-735), one week before this research.
constraints.implication: The proposal must build the principal-keyed vault on the Identity Vault, not introduce a competing CredentialVault; the 'dual-read migration' targets the Redis hot cache key, not the durable store.

constraints.statement: ai-parrot core must never import ai-parrot-server (parrot.services.*); the sink is injected through the CredentialSink Protocol, but parrot/auth/routes.py already lazily imports integrations modules.
constraints.implication: Channel notification must stay behind a Protocol/registry in core; the Jira callback's lazy integrations imports are existing debt to remove, not a pattern to copy.

constraints.statement: auth.user_identities.user_id is a bigint FK to auth.users; channel callbacks must carry the Navigator id under a dedicated nav_user_id state key and never reuse state['user_id'] (the channel id); the table already allows several accounts per provider per user.
constraints.implication: The (principal, provider, account) key the brainstorm wants already matches the schema; the migration risk is principal resolution, not storage.

constraints.statement: Two incompatible principal notions coexist: the broker's CanonicalIdentityMapper (Entra OID → email) and the identity layer's Navigator bigint user_id; FEAT-729 proved they can be bridged at login (provider_user_id == oid).
constraints.implication: One principal key must be chosen for the vault and a mapping step added for the other; otherwise cross-surface reuse silently breaks.

constraints.statement: On Telegram, PermissionContext.user_id is the raw telegram_id and the nav link exists only after /login, persisted to auth.user_identities only as a side effect of the combined Jira flow.
constraints.implication: Zero-reconnect is achievable only for users who linked via /login; others hold only the channel-keyed Redis copy and need a one-time link step.

constraints.statement: FEAT-144 explicitly decided per-(user, agent, toolkit) enablement and declared cross-channel credential sharing a non-goal; IntegrationsService hard-codes channel='web' and is agent-scoped.
constraints.implication: The brainstorm's core goal reverses a recorded product decision; the proposal must state the reversal explicitly and keep per-agent enablement as a separate concern from the connection itself.

constraints.statement: AbstractOAuth2Manager and vault_utils key everything by (provider, channel, user_id) (Redis oauth2:{p}:{c}:{u}, vault oauth2_{p}_{c}_{u}); JiraOAuthManager duplicates the same shape with jira:* keys and is deliberately not a subclass.
constraints.implication: Re-keying is a change in one base class plus a Jira migration onto it — not a new ConnectionManager.

constraints.statement: Completion → channel is a direct in-process dispatch in the callback handlers (app['jira_oauth_notifier'], Slack/Teams handlers, web postMessage); navigator-eventbus is a live dependency used publish-only (Streams) but no channel wrapper subscribes to any topic.
constraints.implication: Event-driven completion requires either a consuming bus instance in channel processes (new wiring) or an in-process notifier registry; the callback and the Telegram bot currently share one aiohttp app.

constraints.statement: UserSocketManager.send_direct_message is process-local and keyed by JWT username, not nav user_id; Redis pubsub exists for channels only.
constraints.implication: Web push of connection.completed needs a username↔principal map and a Redis-backed per-user channel or must stay popup-only.

constraints.statement: Two needs-auth signals: AuthorizationRequired (legacy _pre_execute path) is converted to ToolResult(status='authorization_required', metadata={auth_url, provider, scopes, tool_name}) by ToolManager and to AuthRequiredEnvelope by AgentTalk; CredentialRequired (broker seam) bubbles uncaught by server handlers.
constraints.implication: Unification is a ToolManager-level catch for CredentialRequired producing the same ToolResult, plus retiring one of the two raise sites; both classes live in core.

constraints.statement: JiraToolkit does not declare credential_provider and still uses the FEAT-083 hot-swap placeholder (JiraConnectTool); Office365Toolkit declares credential_provider='o365'.
constraints.implication: Putting Jira on the broker seam (declare-once, resolve-at-call) removes the hot-swap and aligns it with O365.

constraints.statement: MCP per-user tokens are injected at call time via header_provider(ReadonlyContext) (FEAT-264 M9), but token_supplier is zero-arg and MCPClientConfig.user_id / add_oauth_mcp_server(user_id=...) still bind the user at add-time; the MCP auth surface has had zero commits in 120 days.
constraints.implication: The MCP change is removing the add-time user_id and routing token_supplier through the broker — small, no concurrent-edit risk.

constraints.statement: The web integrations API already derives the principal from the authenticated session and validates return_origin against WEB_OAUTH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS; a generic per-provider callback with web postMessage, A2A resume and navigator-auth exclude_list exists at /api/auth/oauth2/{provider}/callback.
constraints.implication: Brainstorm items 7 (routes) and the callback are largely present; the delta is a user-level (non-agent) listing and the Jira route retirement.

constraints.statement: Name collisions: OAuth2ProviderRegistry (core, tool credentials) vs OAUTH2_PROVIDERS (integrations, login IdPs) vs proposed OAuthProviderRegistry; two setup_oauth2_routes (core tool-credential callback vs Telegram WebApp login callback).
constraints.implication: The proposal must reuse the existing names or choose unambiguous new ones; it must not introduce a third registry.

constraints.statement: O365 has three store paths: 3LO browser flow writes vault_utils oauth2_o365_web_{user_id}; device-code CLI writes VaultTokenSync o365:*; Gen-1 /api/v1/o365/auth/sessions routes were deleted (no /api/o365/oauth/* exists).
constraints.implication: The 'microsoft' descriptor the brainstorm plans for S-3a already exists (O365OAuthManager + O365OAuth2Provider); S-3a's O365 work is store consolidation, not a new provider.

constraints.statement: MS Teams already has a user-auth lane (FEAT-729: MSTeamsAuthStrategy, TokenExchangeClient, /login, aad_object_id ↔ nav_user_id) and proactive Jira notifications (FEAT-225); Slack has /connect_jira + DM notifier; Slack first-link still has no owner.
constraints.implication: S-3b's dependency on TeamsHumanChannel is moot; Teams is a channel adapter over existing primitives. Slack should be in scope as a fourth channel.

constraints.statement: Audit must go through parrot.security.audit_ledger.AuditLedger (canonical, KMS-signed); the legacy parrot/auth/audit.py is still imported by msagentsdk/wrapper.py.
constraints.implication: connection.* audit entries target the canonical ledger; the legacy import is pre-existing debt.

constraints.statement: Provider behaviour is code today (AbstractOAuth2Manager subclass per provider + OAuth2Provider metadata subclass); only MCP has descriptor-as-data (MCPOAuth2Config presets); the broker has a YAML manifest loader for per-agent credential configs.
constraints.implication: 'Provider behaviour is data, not code' is a genuine new capability; it can be layered on the manager hooks (endpoints, PKCE flag, extra params, identity probe) without replacing the registry.

new: Principal-keyed credential path: AbstractOAuth2Manager (and the Jira manager once migrated) key Redis/vault entries by the Navigator principal, with channel kept as an attribute and resolved from the channel id through auth.user_identities at the start of a tool call (one lookup, cached per session).

Channel-neutral connections facade: evolve IntegrationsService into a user-level service (list_for_principal / start(provider, principal, channel, return_to) / disconnect / status) and expose it as /api/v1/connections* alongside the agent-scoped /api/v1/agents/integrations routes (which keep per-agent enablement).

connection.completed / connection.revoked / connection.refresh_failed events: published from the generic callback and refresh paths following the fanout.py publish-only Streams pattern, plus an in-core ChannelNotifier Protocol registry so channel adapters (telegram, slack, msteams, web) register notify() once instead of being imported by the callback.
Generic channel commands: /connect <provider>, /disconnect <provider>, /status driven by OAuth2ProviderRegistry (keep /connect_jira and /connect_office365 as aliases).
Unified needs-auth contract: ToolManager converts CredentialRequired to the same ToolResult(status='authorization_required') shape, and the server handlers stop special-casing one exception.

Descriptor-as-data layer: OAuth2Provider / AbstractOAuth2Manager accept endpoint, PKCE, refresh-policy, identity-probe and extra-param configuration from a descriptor (Pydantic + optional YAML), so adding Atlassian/Microsoft/NetSuite does not require a manager subclass.
Web push on completion: a Redis-backed per-principal channel in UserSocketManager so the Connections panel flips without a reload, and an automatic retry hook after connect.

modified.change: principal-keyed key templates with channel as attribute; provider revoke endpoint hook; event publication after handle_callback/_refresh_tokens/revoke; descriptor-driven endpoints

re-implement as an AbstractOAuth2Manager subclass (accessible-resources→cloud_id as a post-exchange hook), keep the CredentialSink, dual-read jira:oauth:{channel}:{user_id} during the migration window
retire /api/auth/jira/callback in favour of the generic /api/auth/oauth2/jira/callback; remove core→integrations lazy imports
publish connection.completed and dispatch via the ChannelNotifier registry for non-web channels instead of web-only branching
channel parameter instead of hard-coded 'web'; principal-level listing; one status probe path (Identity Vault / manager.is_connected) for every provider
also catch CredentialRequired → ToolResult(status='authorization_required'); invalidate per-session resolver caches on connection.completed
declare credential_provider='jira' so the broker seam applies; drop the hot-swap placeholder dependency
remove add-time user_id binding; token_supplier receives the per-call context / resolves through the broker
register every configured provider (o365, mcp, …) from descriptors, not only Jira
Redis-backed send-to-principal across processes; map username↔nav user_id
generic /connect <provider> commands + ChannelNotifier implementation; nav principal resolution from TelegramUserSession / auth.user_identities
becomes the Teams ChannelNotifier; same for slack/oauth_callback.py
user-level Connections panel (status, account, scopes, expiry) fed by /api/v1/connections, WS-driven refresh, auto-retry after ConnectIntegrationPill

untouched: OAuthRoutesMixin on HttpMCPServer and the navigator-auth OAuth 2.1 authorization server (parrot as resource server — opposite direction).
The FEAT-735 ownership decision (Identity Vault durable owner, Redis live path, G4 no per-call Postgres decrypt) and the IdentityVaultCredentialSink.
VaultTokenSync usage for fireflies / workiq / entra device-code and the BYOK per-user LLM keys.
A2A suspend/resume (SuspendedExecutionStore, register_a2a_resume_hook) and the MSAgentSDK Adaptive/OAuth card lane.
Per-(user, agent, toolkit) enablement rows (user_agent_toolkits) — enablement stays per agent even when the connection becomes per principal.
CredentialBroker / CredentialResolverFactory / CanonicalIdentityMapper internals (only consumed; the principal mapping is added around them).

patterns.pattern: Protocol-based injection from server into core (CredentialSink on JiraOAuthManager) — reuse for ChannelNotifier and the principal resolver.
Publish-only Streams EventBus with redacted payloads and durable outbox (observability/fanout.py).
Principal from the authenticated session, never from the body; return_origin allowlist (IntegrationsHandler, IntegrationsService.start_connect).
Manager hooks (_exchange_code, _refresh_request, _discover_identity, _build_token_set, authorization_url_extra_params) as the extension seam for provider behaviour.
nav_user_id travels in OAuth extra_state under its own key; callbacks fail closed on a non-numeric id.
Proactive channel notification keyed by a serialized ConversationReference (Teams) / chat_id (Telegram) stored in extra_state.

risks.risk: Reversing FEAT-144's channel-separate credential decision changes who can use a connection; without an explicit product statement the migration can be read as a security regression.
risks.mitigation: Record the reversal in the spec; keep per-agent enablement; PBAC allowlist on connect.

risks.risk: Two principal keys (Entra OID/email vs Navigator bigint) — picking one strands the other surfaces (A2A/MSAgentSDK vs Telegram/Teams/web).
risks.mitigation: Choose Navigator user_id as the vault key and map OID/email → user_id via auth.user_identities (FEAT-729 bridge).

risks.risk: Telegram users who connected Jira without /login have no principal; zero-reconnect is impossible for them.
risks.mitigation: Dual-read by channel key + one-time /login link prompt; measure legacy-key reads before cutover.

risks.risk: Re-keying the Redis hot cache (jira:oauth:*, oauth2:*) and vault names (oauth2_{p}_{c}_{u}) invalidates live sessions if not dual-read.
risks.mitigation: Read new key, fall back to legacy key, rewrite; delete after a measured window.

risks.risk: Event-driven completion assumes a consumer in the channel bot process; today the Telegram bot and the callback share one aiohttp app and the bus is publish-only.
risks.mitigation: In-process ChannelNotifier registry as the primary path, bus publication for audit/out-of-process consumers; do not block notification on the bus.

risks.risk: Web push requires UserSocketManager changes (cross-process, username vs user_id).
risks.mitigation: Keep popup postMessage as the load-bearing path; WS push is additive.

risks.risk: Name collisions with existing registries/routes (OAuth2ProviderRegistry, OAUTH2_PROVIDERS, two setup_oauth2_routes).
risks.mitigation: Reuse existing names; no new OAuthProviderRegistry.

unknowns.question: Which key is THE principal for the connections vault: the Navigator bigint user_id (used by auth.user_identities, VaultTokenSync and the Telegram/Teams/web lanes) or the broker's canonical Entra OID/email (used by A2A/MSAgentSDK/CLI)?
plausible_answers: Navigator user_id, with OID/email → user_id mapped through auth.user_identities (FEAT-729 bridge)
Entra OID/email, with Telegram/Teams/web mapping their nav user to an OID/email at login
Both, stored as separate columns with the Navigator id as primary
unknowns.user_answer: Both columns, Navigator primary — the connection row stores the navigator-auth bigint user_id (lookup key) and the Entra OID/email as a secondary index for Copilot/A2A/MSAgentSDK surfaces.

unknowns.question: Do you confirm reversing the FEAT-144 decision: a connection belongs to the principal and is usable on every channel and every agent (per-agent toolkit enablement stays as a separate switch)?

unknowns.user_answer: Reverse fully: one connection, all agents — a connected provider is available to every agent the principal can reach on every channel; per-agent enablement (user_agent_toolkits) is dropped.

Keep channel-keyed fallback indefinitely for Telegram
unknowns.user_answer: Force re-connect — Telegram users who connected Jira without /login re-authorize once the principal key is live; no indefinite channel-keyed fallback. Users who linked via /login keep their Identity Vault copy (no reconnect).

Bus is the only path; add consuming bus instances to every channel wrapper
Keep direct calls, just move them behind a Protocol
unknowns.user_answer: Notifier registry + publish-only bus — an in-core ChannelNotifier Protocol registry is the delivery path; connection.* events are also published on the Streams bus for audit/out-of-process consumers, never load-bearing.
